details:
Implementation Plan

The heal intake now only reads the logs of the failed jobs, and the diagnosis runs without network access. The plan has the intake follow same-repository run links found in those logs and give the model their step timelines. In the release gate, only Phase 3b (Implement) and Phase 4 (Review) can print watched run URLs without new API calls. The Clarify and Plan loops don't hold a run id while they poll, so they stay as they are.

## Files likely to change

- `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`
- `scripts/stable_e2e_step_wait_review.sh`
- `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`
- `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`
- `prompts/mode-workflow-failure-heal.txt`
- `prompts/_templates/mode-workflow-failure-heal.txt`
- `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py`
- `tests/test_test_and_mark_stable_plan_polling_guard.py`
- `changelog.d/8248-heal-intake-linked-runs.md` (new)
- `agents.d/8248-heal-intake-linked-runs.md` (new)

## Functions or modules to implement

Planning ref: `main` at `39800b52ff4f64692de7e148408bf67edfd42b25`.

**Release gate: Phase 3b "Wait for implementation" step in `test-and-mark-stable.yml`**

- Add a helper `e2e_note_watched_run <id> <label>`, defined in the step next to `scoped_implement_progress_counts`:
  - It does nothing unless `<id>` is all digits.
  - It keeps a list `E2E_WATCHED_RUN_IDS` of at most 5 entries, newest last.
  - The first time it sees an id, it prints `  ↳ Watching <label> run <id>: https://github.com/${TEST_REPO}/actions/runs/<id>`.
- Add a helper `e2e_watched_run_urls`. It prints ` (watched runs: <url> <url> …)`, or nothing when the list is empty.
- In each poll iteration, after `scoped_implement_progress_counts` and after the by-id check, call `e2e_note_watched_run` for `IMPL_RUN_ID_LATEST`, `SCOPED_IMPL_RUN_ID` and `SCOPED_IMPL_ACTIVE_ID`. Also call it for `IMPL_RUN_ID_WORKING` if #8243 has landed by implement time. All of these values are already fetched, so there are no new API calls.
- Add `$(e2e_watched_run_urls)` to the end of two lines. All existing text stays as it is:
  - `::error::Implement phase stalled — no activity for ${PHASE_TIMEOUT} minutes`
  - the `::error::All ${SCOPED_IMPL_RUN_TOTAL} implement workflow run(s) completed but no PR was created …` line.

**Release gate: Phase 4 step script `scripts/stable_e2e_step_wait_review.sh`**

- Add the same two helpers, with label `Review`. Call `e2e_note_watched_run "$RUN_ID" Review` right after `RUN_ID` is read (around line 456). `RUN_ID` can be `unknown`, which the digit check ignores.
- Append `$(e2e_watched_run_urls)` to `::error::Review phase stalled — no activity for ${REVIEW_TIMEOUT} minutes` (line 826) and to any other `::error::` in that script that reports a timeout or a deadline.

**`scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`**

- `select_linked_runs(texts, repo, exclude_run_ids, limit) -> list[dict]`
  - Calls `extract_run_refs(texts, repo, limit=10_000)`, so the cap is applied only after exclusion.
  - Drops ids in `exclude_run_ids` and returns the last `limit`, newest mention last.
  - Returns `[]` when `limit <= 0`.
- `stall_window_minutes(texts) -> list[int]` reads the stall windows named in the parent's failing-step logs. It matches `no activity for N minutes`, `N-min stall window`, `stall window of N min` and `stall(ed)? … N minutes`, all case-insensitive, with N from 1 to 1440.
- `render_linked_run_timeline(run, jobs, *, repo, run_id, stall_minutes, long_step_secs=600) -> dict`
  - Checks identity: the response's `id` must equal `run_id`, and `repository.full_name` must equal `repo` (compared case-insensitively).
  - Returns `{"ok": false, "reason": "other_repository" | "run_malformed" | "jobs_malformed"}` on failure.
  - Otherwise returns `{"ok": true, "text", "longest": {"job_id", "start", "end"} | null}`.
  - The text has a header (run URL, workflow name, status/conclusion, created and updated times). Under it goes one block per job: job name, conclusion, then one line per step that is not `skipped`, with name, start, end, duration and conclusion.
  - A step still running gets the run's `updated_at` as its end, marked `(still running)`.
  - A line is marked `[LONG]` when its duration is at least `long_step_secs`, or longer than the shortest stall window found.
  - Names are sanitized: control characters removed, whitespace collapsed, 120 characters at most. Caps: 20 jobs, 40 steps per job, 8 KiB of text per run. When `jobs.total_count > 100`, a "truncated" note is added.
- `slice_log_to_window(text, start, end) -> str` keeps the log lines whose leading Actions timestamp (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffffffZ `) falls between `start` and `end`. If no line can be parsed or matched, it returns the whole text unchanged.
- New CLI subcommands, built on the existing `sub.add_parser` pattern:
  - `linked-runs --log-files … --repo R --exclude-run-ids CSV --limit N` prints a JSON list.
  - `linked-run-timeline --run-json --jobs-json --repo --run-id --stall-hint-files …` prints the dict as JSON and always exits 0.
  - `log-window --log-file --start --end` prints the sliced text.

**`scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`**

- Add two settings to the header comment and the defaults block:
  - `MAX_LINKED_RUNS="$(_positive_or_default "${WORKFLOW_HEAL_MAX_LINKED_RUNS:-}" 4)"`. `0` turns the feature off, since `_positive_or_default` accepts `0`.
  - `LINKED_RUN_LOG_BYTES="$(_positive_or_default "${WORKFLOW_HEAL_LINKED_RUN_LOG_BYTES:-}" 30000)"`.
- Add a new function `_heal_collect_linked_runs`. It is called once, after the scope freeze (`SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN`, around line 2325) and before `PROMPT_FILE` is assembled. It writes `${RUNTIME_DIR}/linked_run_timelines.txt`. All of its files live under `${RUNTIME_DIR}/linked_runs/`, never under `${LOG_DIR}`.
  - Its docstring states the API budget: at most 3 REST calls per linked run (run, jobs, one job log), so at most `3 × WORKFLOW_HEAL_MAX_LINKED_RUNS` per intake, and 0 when no link is found. It also states that it fails open.
  - Inputs: the filtered log files listed in `SUMMARIES_FILE` (`.log_file`), and the exclusion list from `jq '.run_refs[].run_id' "${PAYLOAD_FILE}"`.
  - For each linked run, in order:
    1. `gh_api_json_to_file … actions/runs/<id>`.
    2. `gh_api_json_to_file … actions/runs/<id>/jobs -F per_page=100`.
    3. `linked-run-timeline`.
    4. If `longest` is set, fetch the log the same way as the existing loop (`gh api --allow-escape-sequences …/actions/jobs/<id>/logs | redact-stream > raw`). Then run `log-window`, then `filter-log --max-bytes "${LINKED_RUN_LOG_BYTES}"`, then remove the raw file.
    5. Pass the rendered timeline text through `redact-stream` as well.
  - Each failure logs `WORKFLOW_HEAL warn linked_run_skipped run=<id> reason=<token>` and goes on to the next run. The reasons are `run_unreadable`, `run_malformed`, `other_repository`, `jobs_unreadable`, `jobs_malformed` and `timeline_failed`.
  - A failed log read keeps the timeline, writes `(job log unavailable)` and logs `reason=log_unavailable`.
  - The call site is `_heal_collect_linked_runs || log "warn linked_runs_failed"`.
- In prompt assembly, before `echo "=== FAILED RUN LOGS (UNTRUSTED) ==="`: when `linked_run_timelines.txt` is non-empty, print `=== LINKED RUN TIMELINES (UNTRUSTED) ===`, then the file, then a blank line.

**`prompts/mode-workflow-failure-heal.txt` and its `_templates` copy (kept byte-identical)**

- Add an Inputs bullet for the `LINKED RUN TIMELINES` block. It covers runs that the failed logs link to, their step timelines with `[LONG]` steps, and the log window of the longest step. The block appears only when links exist.
- Add instructions:
  - Check the linked timelines before blaming a stall or a missing artefact on the polling run.
  - When a needed run is still missing, name its run id in the diagnosis instead of writing "not in the evidence".

## Data structures affected

- New files in the runtime directory only: `${RUNTIME_DIR}/linked_runs/run-<id>.json`, `run-<id>-jobs.json`, `run-<id>-job-<job>.txt`, and `${RUNTIME_DIR}/linked_run_timelines.txt`.
- No change to the payload schema, `SUMMARIES_FILE`, `LOG_FILES`, `SCOPE_INPUTS_FROZEN`, fingerprints, or any marker.
- Release gate: step-local shell variable `E2E_WATCHED_RUN_IDS`. No change to step outputs.

## API or interface changes

- New environment variables with defaults set in the script (§8): `WORKFLOW_HEAL_MAX_LINKED_RUNS` (default 4, `0` turns it off) and `WORKFLOW_HEAL_LINKED_RUN_LOG_BYTES` (default 30000). No workflow file forwards them.
- New CLI subcommands of `workflow_failure_heal.py`: `linked-runs`, `linked-run-timeline`, `log-window`.
- New log line under the existing `WORKFLOW_HEAL` prefix: `warn linked_run_skipped run= reason=`. No new prefix to register.
- New prompt section: `=== LINKED RUN TIMELINES (UNTRUSTED) ===`.
- Release-gate `::error::` lines only gain text at the end.

## Decisions

### D1 — Where linked runs are collected

- **Chosen:** after the scope freeze and right before the prompt is assembled, with all files under `${RUNTIME_DIR}/linked_runs/`.
- **Alternatives considered:** inside the job loop around lines 1444-1494, or writing the files into `${LOG_DIR}`.
- **Why:** the scope freeze reads the globs `${LOG_DIR}/run-*-job-*.txt` and `${LOG_DIR}/*.verified`, and `LOG_FILES` feeds the error signature. Collecting later, in a separate directory, means linked data can never widen the heal scope or change the fingerprint (#6463). It also spends no API calls on reports that end before the diagnosis (duplicates, skips).

### D2 — Long-step threshold

- **Chosen:** mark a step when its duration is at least 600 seconds, or longer than the shortest stall window named in the parent's failing logs.
- **Alternatives considered:** comparing against the longest stall window, or only the fixed 10 minutes.
- **Why:** "longer than any" is read as "longer than at least one". This catches the #8244 case of a 31-minute step against a 30-m
